subject: maths
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF

topics.title: Number sequences: odd, even, triangular, square, cube
outcomes: Learner can recognise and extend important number sequences and describe the rule in words
misconceptions: Believes a sequence is determined by its first two terms only
hooks: Stacking laddoos into triangles; square tiles in a courtyard

topics.title: Visualising sequences with pictures
outcomes: Learner can draw dot pictures that explain why a sequence grows the way it does
misconceptions: Thinks pictures are decoration and cannot prove anything
hooks: Arrange 1, 4, 9, 16 coins as squares on a table

topics.title: Relations among sequences
outcomes: Learner can explain relationships such as "adding consecutive odd numbers gives square numbers" using pictures
misconceptions: Assumes a pattern seen in three cases is true for all cases without reasoning
hooks: 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = ? build L-shapes of rangoli dots

topics.title: Patterns in shapes
outcomes: Learner can identify number sequences hidden in shape patterns (polygons, stacked squares, Koch snowflake)
misconceptions: Thinks shape patterns and number patterns are unrelated
hooks: Count sides in regular polygons; count lines in a star pattern

topics.title: Point, line segment, line and ray
outcomes: Learner can distinguish a point, line segment, line and ray and name them using letters
misconceptions: Thinks a line drawn longer is a different (bigger) line
Believes a ray has two endpoints
hooks: Torch beam as a ray; edge of a ruler as a segment

topics.title: Angles and comparing angles
outcomes: Learner can describe an angle as an amount of turn between two rays from a common vertex and compare angles
misconceptions: Believes an angle with longer arms is bigger
hooks: Opening of a door, hands of a clock, a pair of scissors

topics.title: Measuring and drawing angles
outcomes: Learner can measure and draw angles using a protractor, reading the correct scale
misconceptions: Reads the wrong scale on the protractor (gets 130° for a 50° angle)
hooks: Measure the angle of a slide in the park

topics.title: Types of angles
outcomes: Learner can classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex by their measure
misconceptions: Thinks a straight line cannot be an angle
hooks: Angles made by roads at a crossing

topics.title: Numbers that tell us things
outcomes: Learner can solve number puzzles such as supercells and explain the reasoning
misconceptions: Assumes there is only one correct answer to every puzzle
hooks: Children in a line say how many taller neighbours they have

topics.title: Playing with digits and palindromes
outcomes: Learner can explore digit sums, palindromes and the Kaprekar routine and make conjectures
misconceptions: Believes a pattern that works for a few numbers must always work
hooks: Palindromic dates and vehicle number plates

topics.title: Number patterns and the Collatz conjecture
outcomes: Learner can carry out a number rule repeatedly and describe what happens
misconceptions: Thinks every mathematical question already has a known answer
hooks: The Collatz game: halve if even, 3n + 1 if odd

topics.title: Estimation and mental maths
outcomes: Learner can estimate large quantities and use mental strategies to calculate quickly
misconceptions: Thinks an estimate is useless unless it is exact
hooks: How many people in a cricket stadium? how many words in a newspaper?

topics.title: Collecting and organising data
outcomes: Learner can collect data to answer a question and organise it in a frequency table with tallies
misconceptions: Thinks raw data in a list is already "organised"
hooks: Favourite sport survey in your colony

topics.title: Pictographs
outcomes: Learner can draw and interpret pictographs with a suitable key
misconceptions: Ignores the key and counts symbols as single items
hooks: Number of trees planted by each class on Van Mahotsav

topics.title: Bar graphs
outcomes: Learner can draw bar graphs with a suitable scale and interpret them
misconceptions: Makes bars of different widths or uneven gaps and thinks it does not matter
Chooses a scale that does not start at zero and misreads differences
hooks: Runs scored by batters in an IPL match

topics.title: Common factors and common multiples
outcomes: Learner can find common factors and common multiples using games and lists
misconceptions: Confuses factors with multiples
hooks: Idli-vada game: say "idli" on multiples of 3, "vada" on multiples of 5

topics.title: Prime and composite numbers
outcomes: Learner can identify primes up to 100 using the sieve of Eratosthenes and explain why 1 is not prime
misconceptions: Believes all odd numbers are prime
Thinks 1 is a prime number
hooks: Arrange chairs: which numbers can only make one row?

topics.title: Co-prime numbers
outcomes: Learner can decide whether two numbers are co-prime
misconceptions: Thinks co-prime numbers must both be prime
hooks: Co-prime lock combinations for a treasure box

topics.title: Prime factorisation
outcomes: Learner can write a number as a product of primes using a factor tree
misconceptions: Stops the factor tree at a composite number
hooks: Break 360 (degrees in a circle) into primes

topics.title: Divisibility tests
outcomes: Learner can use divisibility tests for 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10 and explain why some work
misconceptions: Believes a number is divisible by 4 if its last digit is 4
hooks: Can 144 laddoos be packed in boxes of 9?

topics.title: Perimeter of rectangles, squares and polygons
outcomes: Learner can find the perimeter of shapes and derive formulas for rectangles and squares
misconceptions: Adds only length and breadth once
hooks: Fencing a vegetable patch; running around a park

topics.title: Area of rectangles and squares
outcomes: Learner can find area by counting squares and using length × breadth, with correct square units
misconceptions: Writes area in cm instead of square cm
Thinks shapes with equal perimeters have equal areas
hooks: Tiles needed for a room floor

topics.title: Area of a triangle
outcomes: Learner can explain why a triangle’s area is half of a related rectangle
misconceptions: Believes the area of a triangle is length × breadth
hooks: Cut a paper rectangle along its diagonal

topics.title: Fractional units and equal shares
outcomes: Learner can describe fractional units (1/2, 1/3, 1/4 ...) as equal parts of a whole and measure with them
misconceptions: Thinks the parts of a whole need not be equal
Believes 1/5 > 1/3 because 5 > 3
hooks: Sharing rotis among siblings; a measuring tape in fractions of a metre

topics.title: Fractions on the number line and mixed fractions
outcomes: Learner can place proper and improper fractions on a number line and convert to mixed fractions
misconceptions: Thinks fractions can only be less than 1
hooks: How many 1/4 kg packets in 2 1/2 kg of rice?

topics.title: Equivalent fractions
outcomes: Learner can generate equivalent fractions and reduce a fraction to lowest terms
misconceptions: Adds the same number to numerator and denominator to get equivalent fractions (1/2 = 2/3)
hooks: 1/2 a chapati = 2/4 of it

topics.title: Comparing fractions
outcomes: Learner can compare fractions by converting to equivalent fractions with a common denominator
misconceptions: Compares only numerators or only denominators
hooks: Who ate more: 3/4 of a dosa or 2/3?

topics.title: Adding and subtracting fractions
outcomes: Learner can add and subtract fractions with like and unlike denominators
misconceptions: Adds numerators and denominators separately (1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5)
hooks: Brahmagupta’s method; mixing 1/2 litre milk and 1/4 litre water

topics.title: Circles with a compass
outcomes: Learner can draw circles and arcs with a compass and explain radius as distance from the centre
misconceptions: Thinks the radius changes depending on where you measure
hooks: Drawing a rangoli with a string and chalk

topics.title: Constructing squares and rectangles
outcomes: Learner can construct squares and rectangles with given sides using a ruler and compass
misconceptions: Believes a quadrilateral with four equal sides is always a square
hooks: Mark a badminton court with chalk

topics.title: Diagonals and equidistant points
outcomes: Learner can explore properties of diagonals of rectangles and find points equidistant from two given points
misconceptions: Thinks diagonals of every rectangle meet at right angles
hooks: Where should the water tank go so two houses are equally far?

topics.title: Line symmetry
outcomes: Learner can identify and draw lines of symmetry in figures and alphabets
misconceptions: Believes a rectangle’s diagonals are lines of symmetry
hooks: Taj Mahal front view; butterfly wings; Ashoka emblem

topics.title: Rotational symmetry
outcomes: Learner can find the angle and order of rotational symmetry of figures
misconceptions: Thinks a figure with no line symmetry cannot have rotational symmetry
hooks: Ceiling fan blades; the chakra in the flag

topics.title: Integers in everyday life
outcomes: Learner can represent situations like floors below ground, temperatures and money owed using integers
misconceptions: Believes negative numbers are not "real" numbers
hooks: Lift buttons B1, B2 in a mall; Leh temperatures in winter

topics.title: Integers on the number line and comparison
outcomes: Learner can place integers on a number line and compare them
misconceptions: Thinks -7 is greater than -2 because 7 > 2
hooks: Which is colder: -5 °C in Drass or -2 °C in Shimla?

topics.title: Adding and subtracting integers (token model)
outcomes: Learner can add and subtract integers using positive and negative tokens and the number line
misconceptions: Believes subtracting always makes a number smaller (even 3 - (-2))
Thinks two negatives always make a positive, even in addition
hooks: Bank deposits and withdrawals; a lift going up and down
